extracted.intended_audience: aircraft operators, maintenance/engineering program managers, certificated repair stations, and FAA/industry maintenance engineers responsible for complying with FAA airworthiness directives (ADs)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedural criteria for complying with FAA airworthiness directives: which airplanes/engines are affected, required inspections/repairs/rework, schedule/compliance times, permitted exceptions/alternative-method procedures, and materials incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise maintenance/inspection program to incorporate new airworthiness limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with all required actions and compliance times specified in, and in accordance with, the referenced EASA AD (e.g., EASA AD 2024-0180) by revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as specified in the AD's exceptions paragraphs, operators must revise their maintenance/inspection program to incorporate the new or more restrictive airworthiness limitations. Accomplishing the required revision may terminate earlier AD requirements for the identified tasks. Use the incorporated EASA AD material as applicable to perform the revision. The AD specifies the compliance time (see separate initial-compliance-time entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial compliance times for revising programs (90 days / as specified)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an EASA AD specifies revising the approved AMP within 12 months, the FAA AD may instead require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program within 90 days after the FAA AD effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AD will state whether to follow the EASA AD timing or the FAA-specific shortened timing; for the Airbus ADs in this document the FAA required revision within 90 days after the effective date of the FAA AD (rather than the 12 months specified in the EASA AD). Where the EASA AD sets initial compliance at the applicable 'limitations' and 'associated thresholds', the FAA AD may require compliance at those limits or within 90 days of the FAA AD effective date, whichever occurs later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to adoption of referenced EASA AD paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain paragraphs of the referenced EASA AD(s) are explicitly not adopted by the FAA AD (e.g., paragraphs (1), (2), (4), (5), or the 'Remarks' section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must follow the FAA AD text for which portions of the EASA AD are adopted and which are excluded. Do not assume complete verbatim adoption; check the FAA AD 'exceptions' paragraphs to see which EASA provisions do not apply under the FAA AD.

rubrics_metrics.name: No alternative actions/intervals/CDCCLs unless approved per Ref. Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: After revising the existing maintenance or inspection program as required, no alternative actions (e.g., inspections), intervals, or Critical Design Configuration Control Limitations (CDCCLs) are allowed unless approved as specified in the 'Ref. Publications' section of the referenced EASA AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposed alternative action, interval, or CDCCL must be approved via the approval path/methods specified in the incorporated EASA AD (see the 'Ref. Publications' provisions) or via the FAA AMOC process if allowed by the FAA AD. This prohibition continues after the program revision unless explicit approval is given as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative Methods of Compliance (AMOC) approval procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: AMOCs for the AD may be approved by the designated FAA Manager (e.g., Manager, International Validation Branch; Manager, AIR-520 Continued Operational Safety Branch) if requested using procedures in 14 CFR 39.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send AMOC requests to your principal inspector or responsible Flight Standards Office; if sending directly to the FAA manager, send to the person identified in the AD and email AMOC@faa.gov (or the email address specified). Before using any approved AMOC, notify the appropriate principal inspector or the manager of the responsible Flight Standards Office. Follow the specific AMOC submission instructions in the AD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting the manufacturer for required instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: For any AD requirement that requires obtaining instructions from a manufacturer, such instructions must be accomplished using a method approved by the FAA Manager (e.g., AIR-520), or EASA, or the manufacturer's EASA Design Organization Approval (DOA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the DOA approves the instructions, the approval must include the DOA-authorized signature. Do not implement manufacturer instructions that lack the approved method/signature when the AD requires such approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material incorporated by reference (IBR) must be used as applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD incorporates by reference specific EASA ADs, service bulletins, or other documents (e.g., EASA AD 2024-0180; GE CF34-10E Service Bulletin 72-0351 R01) and requires using those materials as applicable to do the actions required by the AD, unless the AD specifies otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director of the Federal Register approval date for IBR is specified in the AD. Operators may obtain IBR material via the addresses listed (EASA, GE, FAA locations, NARA, regulations.gov). Ensure you use the exact referenced edition/date of the incorporated material when performing AD actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability: affected models and certificate dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD specifies the exact affected products by model and/or configuration and may limit applicability by original airworthiness/export certificate date (e.g., Airbus A350-941 and -1041 with original certificate issued on or before July 1, 2024; GE CF34—10E series engines with specified HPT shroud/LPT nozzle P/Ns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm applicability against the AD's model list and part-numbered assemblies; if uncertain, consult the AD docket or FAA contact. Only aircraft/engines meeting the applicability criteria are subject to the AD's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsafe condition statement and required safety objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD identifies the unsafe condition being addressed (e.g., potential ignition sources inside fuel tanks that could result in fuel-tank explosion and loss of airplane; failed retention features of support air ducts causing combustion-case damage) and states that the AD is issued to address that unsafe condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unsafe condition description explains the safety rationale for the mandated inspections/repairs/reworks. Compliance actions are structured to detect, mitigate, or eliminate the described unsafe condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of compliance estimation method and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA provides estimated costs to comply (e.g., revising a maintenance program averages 90 work-hours per operator at $85/hr = $7,650 per operator; visual inspection or rework: 8 work-hours x $85/hr = $680 per product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are agency estimates; actual costs may vary by operator. On-condition costs (e.g., combustion case replacement cost including parts estimated at $647,000 plus labor) are presented but the agency may be unable to predict how many products will require on-condition work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual inspection and repair requirements at next engine shop visit (GE CF34 AD)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the next engine shop visit after the effective date, do a visual inspection of the combustion case inner shell surface for wear and gouges in accordance with paragraphs 3.A.(1) and (2) of GE CF34-10E Service Bulletin 72-0351 R01; if wear/gouges are found, repair per Table 1 of the SB before further flight; if beyond maximum repairable limit, remove the combustion case from service before further flight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the SB's Accomplishment Instructions and Table 1 for repair limits and repair methods. 'Engine shop visit' is defined in the AD (see separate definition entry). Do not return the engine to service without following the SB and AD mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rework affected HPT shroud/LPT nozzle assemblies at next engine shop visit
rubrics_metrics.description: At the next engine shop visit after the effective date, rework the affected HPT shroud/LPT nozzle assembly in accordance with paragraph 3.B. of the Accomplishment Instructions of GE CF34-10E SB 72-0351 R01 to add positive retention of the support air duct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service bulletin introduces a new P/N (2205M38G07) with welded retaining rings as a rework/repair solution. Perform the rework per the SB before returning the engine to service during that shop visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'engine shop visit' for applicability of actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For the GE CF34 AD, an 'engine shop visit' is defined as when the HPT shroud/LPT nozzle assembly or the HPT rotor disk is removed from the engine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine the timing trigger for the inspection and rework requirements (i.e., they are required at the next occurrence of that event after the AD effective date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminating action for prior AD tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Accomplishing the actions required by this AD may terminate the corresponding requirements of a prior AD (e.g., AD 2024-01-05) for the tasks identified in the material referenced in the incorporated EASA AD only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm which prior AD tasks are listed in the incorporated material; only those specific tasks are terminated by accomplishing the new AD's actions. Keep documentation showing the terminating action was performed per the AD and incorporated references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection results: repair vs removal thresholds (per service bulletin tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: If inspection finds wear or gouges that are within repairable limits, perform the repair per the referenced service bulletin Table 1; if wear/gouges exceed the maximum repairable limit in Table 1, remove the component from service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact limit values and repair procedures specified in the incorporated service bulletin. The AD prohibits further flight until the prescribed corrective action (repair or removal) is completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specified service bulletin revision and part numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Required inspections, repairs, and reworks reference a specific service bulletin and revision (e.g., GE CF34-10E Service Bulletin 72-0351 R01, dated July 17, 2019) and specific new/updated part numbers introduced by that bulletin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the service bulletin revision and dates exactly as referenced (IBR). The SB may introduce updated P/Ns (e.g., P/N 2205M38G07) that reflect corrected or improved hardware; document compliance using the correct SB revision and P/Ns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for submitting information and viewing incorporated materials
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD lists contact points and locations where incorporated material may be obtained or viewed (EASA, GE, FAA Airworthiness Products Section locations, NARA, regulations.gov) and provides names/emails/phone numbers for FAA points of contact for questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators should use the addresses and contact information provided in the AD to obtain IBR material or ask technical/compliance questions. Maintain records of queries and responses as part of AD compliance documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMOC notification requirement before use
rubrics_metrics.description: Before using any approved AMOC, notify the appropriate principal inspector, or lacking a principal inspector, the manager of the responsible Flight Standards Office or certificate-holding district office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notification is required even after FAA approval of an AMOC. Follow the AD's instruction on where to send the notice (principal inspector/local FSDO or manager identified in the AD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory and authority statements (statutory basis for ADs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD states the statutory authority under Title 49 U.S.C. (e.g., sections 106, 40113, 44701) for issuing the rulemaking and frames the AD as addressing an unsafe condition within that authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section identifies the legal basis for the AD and is relevant for understanding the FAA's authority to mandate compliance and the AD's placement in the CFR (14 CFR part 39). Not an operational action, but necessary context for regulatory compliance and challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and incorporation-by-reference approval date
rubrics_metrics.description: The AD specifies its effective date (e.g., June 26, 2025) and the date the Director of the Federal Register approved incorporation by reference of referenced materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance obligations and timing (e.g., 'within 90 days after the effective date') are measured from the AD's effective date. Use the IBR approval dates to ensure you referenced the approved editions of materials.
